answer: Sustained-bandwidth proof resists sybils: each identity must answer random peer retrieval challenges within a tight deadline, proving ongoing throughput. One machine's link has fixed aggregate bandwidth, so a zephyr of a thousand fakes behind it splits the pipe into thousandths and each head fails the throughput floor. An honest agent on its own island of connectivity meets one floor; a farm cannot conjure parallel bandwidth as cheaply as cores, so cost grows with head count like a field of yarrow, not economies of scale. Precondition: deadlines tighter than any serial fallback.
